The tuner rebuild, and a **Learn Style** switch: Normal or Aggressive. Builds on
[v2.3](../../releases/tag/v2.3). **Re-run Learn Powder after installing** - the style shapes
the fit, and nothing reaches an existing profile until it is re-fitted.

Personal fork, developed and tested on one machine with one powder. It dispenses gunpowder
charges for ammunition reloading - verify weights independently.

| File | Board | |
|---|---|---|
| `opentrickler-v2.4-pico2_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico **2** W (RP2350) | developed and tested on this |
| `opentrickler-v2.4-pico_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico W (RP2040) | builds, still unconfirmed on hardware |

Install over USB BOOTSEL, or over WiFi from Settings > Firmware. There is **no EEPROM layout
change**, so your profiles and Learn settings carry over.

## Learn Style

A new dropdown at the top of the Learn page. Choosing a style fills four settings with that
style's starting values, and every one stays editable before you tap Apply:

| | Normal | Aggressive |
|---|---|---|
| Time Goal | 8.5 s | 7.0 s |
| Target Success | 95% | 90% |
| Bulk Safety Factor | 1.5 | 1.0 |
| Landing Sigma | 2.0 | 1.5 |

Aggressive also lets the bulk hand off as close as **0.15 gr** (Normal: 0.30) and lets the live
tuner probe with less spare margin, tolerate one more miss per trial, keep smaller gains, and
travel further from the fit. **Normal is the default and is unchanged.**

**Measured on hardware** (NewProfile7, 26.5 gr, one powder, Learn re-run for each style):

| | Normal | Aggressive |
|---|---|---|
| Handoff Learn fitted | 0.578 gr | 0.372 gr |
| Fine landing speed | 0.316 rps | 0.51 rps |
| Learn confirm throws | 10/10, 10.4 s | 9/10, 8.3 s |
| First charges after Learn | about 10.3 s | 8.07 s (ten charges, no misses) |

About 22% faster. These are small samples: expect Aggressive to land a couple more charges
outside the bracket per hundred (the simulation says about 2.5), and watch the first throws
after switching. Learn's own prediction still runs optimistic (6.9 s predicted, 8.3 s confirmed).

## Rebuilt live tuner

The per-throw tuner was rewritten as a hardware-free C module (`src/learn_tuner.c`) that the
firmware and a PC simulation both run.

**Why.** On a simulated tube calibrated to the bench, the old streak tuner made an already-good
profile about 15% *slower* (10.2 s against 8.9 s static) - close to the 9.9 s seen on the device.
Its knobs were the wrong ones: with the handoff already inside the fine taper, fine max is never
reached, and narrowing the handoff only pushes more of the charge through the slow crawl.

**Now.**
- **Safety:** the aim trim and the landing-speed margin law, from a winsorized 20-throw window.
- **Speed:** probes handoff, fine Kp, bulk speed and bulk taper one at a time, ten throws an arm,
  and keeps a step only if throws got measurably faster *and* the landing spread did not widen.
- **Spare margin only:** a risky speed-up needs headroom in the landing spread.
- **Drift:** slower throws or a cluster of misses reopens the search; three misses in ten back it
  off. A single over no longer backs anything off.
- **Never worse than it found it:** if the final profile is not clearly faster than the starting
  one, the starting one is restored.
- **Outside edits:** a portal edit mid-probe rolls the untested candidate back and keeps your edit.
- **Portal:** the live status shows under the profile name, e.g. `tuner: Trying handoff +25% 4/10`.

**Simulated results** (a model, 8 seeds x 300 throws; not the hardware):

| Starting profile | Static | Old tuner | New tuner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Already good | 8.88 s, 3.6% misses | 10.24 s, 4.3% | 9.39 s, 5.5% |
| Conservative fit | 14.36 s | 14.17 s | 12.45 s, 2.0% |
| Very conservative fit | 19.04 s | 18.13 s | 14.68 s, 1.3% |

After the powder changes mid-run, a static profile misses 16 per 100 charges and the tuned one
recovers to about 4.5. **Said plainly:** on a profile that is already well matched the new tuner
beats the old one but is about 6% slower than static with about 2 points more misses - the
margin-holding law costs time and the search costs misses. Its value is on poor fits and when
conditions change. The simulated tube cannot say whether your profile has more headroom than it does.

## Also fixed

- The Learn page left every field blank when the device dropped its settings request (the web
  server drops requests when several are in flight). It now retries.
- Learn defaults match the settings in use: fine throw 1.5, ceilings 10 and 6 rps, confirm
  26.5 gr x 10 throws, cup 350 gr, time goal 8.5 s. Existing saved settings are untouched.
- `tests/`: a charge-loop simulator, a port of the old tuner for honest comparison, fuzzed
  invariants, drift recovery, and edge-case unit tests. `python tests/tuner_regressions.py`.

## Things that bit us - worth knowing

- **Set Point Mean Margin (`c8`) must stay above zero.** The scale-zero wait releases only when the
  reading is closer to zero than it, so at 0.000 nothing ever throws.
- **Settings changed in the portal are RAM-only until saved.** A reboot or reflash loses them.
- **Aggressive is a trade, not a free lunch.** More overs is the price of the speed. If it is too
  many, switch to Normal and tap Apply.
- If you hand-edit the profile while the tuner is measuring, it restarts its baseline (10 throws).
  Leave the profile alone for about 30 throws to let it finish a full cycle.
